findings.title: No test protects the Secretariat projections from sensitive-field regressions
findings.body: Premise: __tests__/admin-actions.test.ts:152-186 exercises getApplications only with the default Administrator mock, while app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:54-69 and :121-140 add the two Secretariat-only allowlist projections → Path: a future change can remove columns/with from either Secretaria branch, or route that role through the full query, while every current test still passes → Verdict: income, documents, CPF/address/receipt data, or other restricted fields can reach a Secretariat client without a failing-capable test. Add role-specific tests that resolve requireCapability as Secretaria and assert the exact application/student and donor query column allowlists (including excluded keys).
evidence: Premise: app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:51-80 contains a Secretaria-only application projection → Path: requireCapability resolves as Secretaria → Verdict: the restricted branch is the privacy boundary.

Premise: app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:117-147 contains a separate Secretaria donor projection → Path: donor list runs for Secretaria → Verdict: the restricted branch is the donor privacy boundary.
Premise: __tests__/admin-actions.test.ts:92-109,152-186 always resolve authorization as admin → Path: the listed getApplications tests execute → Verdict: neither Secretaria projection is exercised.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_02.md:107-119 requires exact allowlists and excluded fields → Path: a sensitive field is added to either projection → Verdict: the current suite has no assertion to fail.

findings.title: Upload tests cover only one category and not the required allowlist boundary
findings.body: Premise: the changed createUploadUrl gate at app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:32-37 accepts eight fixed categories plus two indexed student forms, but __tests__/form-actions.test.ts:63-114 calls it only with rg_pai and has no invalid-category assertion → Path: a typo or future edit that omits certidao, recibo_pagamento, rg_aluno_N, or certidao_nascimento_N (or accepts traversal/separator/non-numeric categories) passes the suite; the client then cannot upload a required document or can receive an unintended ticket → Verdict: the client/server upload contract has no failing-capable protection for most required categories. Table-test every accepted fixed/indexed category and reject unknown, traversal, separator, and malformed-index categories.
evidence: Premise: app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:32-37 is the changed server allowlist gate → Path: createUploadUrl receives a category → Verdict: category acceptance controls ticket issuance.
Premise: app/form/_components/step-2-students.tsx:188,202 uses both indexed student category families → Path: a student uploads either document → Verdict: both allowlist forms must remain accepted.
Premise: __tests__/form-actions.test.ts:63-114 calls createUploadUrl successfully only with rg_pai → Path: another fixed or indexed category regresses → Verdict: the current tests remain green.
Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_05.md:113-119 requires accepted and rejected category coverage → Path: the upload task is accepted → Verdict: the test matrix is incomplete.

findings.title: Birth-certificate persistence is not asserted separately from student identity
findings.body: Premise: app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:288-289 now persists two distinct student-document categories, whereas __tests__/submit-application.test.ts:138-148 asserts only the rg_aluno row → Path: removing or mislabelling the certidao_nascimento addDocs call still satisfies the valid-input test and the sole student-document assertion → Verdict: a required student birth certificate can be dropped or linked incorrectly without a test failure. Assert both rows' categories, final paths, and student_id for one student.
evidence: Premise: app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:285-290 makes identity and birth certificate separate persistence calls → Path: a complete student submission is stored → Verdict: each row requires an independent assertion.
Premise: __tests__/submit-application.test.ts:138-148 locates only categoria === rg_aluno → Path: certidao_nascimento is removed or mislabelled → Verdict: the test still passes.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_05.md:124-125 requires distinct metadata and student linkage → Path: Task 05 is accepted → Verdict: the birth-certificate invariant is unprotected.

findings.title: Não persista o usuário fictício do bypass como emissor
findings.body: Com `AUTH_BYPASS=true` fora de produção, `requireAdmin()` devolve o UUID sentinela que não existe em `admin_users`. A emissão então tenta inserir esse UUID em `issued_documents.issued_by`, que é uma FK obrigatória, e falha. Assim, o modo de desenvolvimento documentado não consegue emitir decisão nem contrato depois da nova persistência.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:534 passes `user.id` to persistence, while lib/auth/authorization.ts:42-43 returns BYPASS_USER with ID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` outside production → Path: an AUTH_BYPASS administrator exports a decided application → Verdict: the required issued_documents.issued_by foreign key rejects the metadata insert and the action returns an issuance error.
lib/auth/bypass.ts:1-7 → the bypass UUID is fixed and is not a database-backed staff identity.
drizzle/0006_flimsy_spacker_dave.sql:30 → issued_documents.issued_by has a required foreign key to admin_users.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:34-40 → the existing decision path already recognizes that the bypass user cannot be stored as a real staff FK.

findings.title: Quick-access order still makes scholarship primary
findings.body: Premise: `app/page.tsx:574-575` renders the scholarship link before `Seja um benfeitor`, while the updated primary navigation (`app/page.tsx:344-347`) and content bands (`app/page.tsx:459-483`) correctly place benefactor enrollment first → Path: a visitor using the footer's ‘Acesso rápido’ follows the remaining public shortcut → Verdict: one of the explicitly required public entry points contradicts the donor-first hierarchy and exposes the secondary scholarship journey first. Swap these two list items so all three hierarchy surfaces use the same order.
evidence: Premise: app/page.tsx:344-350 puts benefactor enrollment first in the primary navigation and CTA → Path: app/page.tsx:574-575 is the footer quick-access route that visitors can use instead → Verdict: it reverses the required primary/secondary order.

Premise: app/page.tsx:459-506 places the benefactor band before the scholarship band → Path: the footer represents the remaining quick-access surface → Verdict: its opposite order leaves the donor-first invariant incomplete.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_04.md:5 requires benefactor enrollment before scholarship in quick access → Path: app/page.tsx:574-575 renders scholarship first → Verdict: the explicit route-hierarchy acceptance criterion fails.

Premise: app/page.tsx:571-576 renders the scholarship quick-access link before the benefactor link → Path: visitors using the landing footer encounter the scholarship journey first → Verdict: the required donor-first quick-access order is violated.
app/page.tsx:571-576 → the footer's `Acesso rápido` list places `/solicitar-bolsa` before `/seja-um-benfeitor`.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_prd.md Core Features 1 → public quick-access links must list benefactor enrollment before scholarship applications.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_04.md requirement 5 → benefactor must precede scholarship in quick access.

findings.title: Canonical donor flow dropped its payment instructions
findings.body: Premise: the legacy donor page removed in this change contained the Pix/transfer account details, while the canonical page now renders only its short header and `DonorForm` at `app/seja-um-benfeitor/page.tsx:12` → Path: the retained form still tells a donor to upload a receipt ‘Após realizar o Pix ou a transferência’ (`app/benfeitor/_components/donor-form.tsx:344`) but provides neither Pix nor transfer destination → Verdict: visitors routed to the new canonical donor journey cannot complete the advertised payment/receipt step. Preserve the institutional and bank-transfer section in the canonical page (or render an equivalent source shared with the form).
evidence: Premise: git diff 5c90842fe230 -- app/benfeitor/page.tsx shows the removed route had ACIPEC/Santander, agency, account, and CNPJ details → Path: the canonical route replaced it → Verdict: the canonical flow lost the payment destination.

Premise: app/seja-um-benfeitor/page.tsx:12 renders only a header and DonorForm → Path: a donor reaches this route through every updated public CTA → Verdict: no payment instructions are available on the new journey.

Premise: app/benfeitor/_components/donor-form.tsx:344 instructs the visitor to send a receipt after Pix or transfer → Path: the form provides no corresponding Pix or transfer destination → Verdict: the payment-and-receipt workflow cannot be completed from the canonical page.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_04.md:1-2 makes the canonical route the donor-enrollment implementation → Path: payment information stayed only in deleted legacy markup → Verdict: the route transition regresses the existing enrollment journey.

findings.title: Canonical scholarship route lost its route metadata
findings.body: Premise: `app/form/page.tsx` is now only a permanent redirect, and its former metadata remains attached to the unused legacy `app/form/layout.tsx`; the new canonical `app/solicitar-bolsa/page.tsx:1-11` exports no `metadata` → Path: requests and crawlers for `/solicitar-bolsa` resolve the canonical page but inherit only root metadata rather than the scholarship-specific title and description → Verdict: the route-transition requirement that canonical metadata describe the correct flow is not met. Move or define the scholarship metadata on the canonical route/layout.
evidence: Premise: app/form/page.tsx:1-5 makes the legacy segment a redirect only → Path: crawlers resolve /solicitar-bolsa as the canonical page → Verdict: metadata scoped only to app/form no longer describes the public destination.

Premise: app/form/layout.tsx:5-9 contains scholarship-specific metadata → Path: app/solicitar-bolsa/page.tsx:1-11 is a separate segment without a metadata export → Verdict: the canonical page inherits generic metadata instead.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_04.md:105-108 requires canonical metadata for the correct flow → Path: the metadata was not moved with the implementation → Verdict: the route-transition acceptance criterion is unmet.

findings.title: Immutable issued-document behavior has no failing-capable tests
findings.body: Premise: lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:9-66 introduces storage writes, compensating deletion, per-kind versioning, current-document selection, and history reads, but no test imports this module or the new getCurrentIssuedDocuments/getIssuedDocumentUrl/getIssuedDocumentHistory actions → Path: deleting the advisory lock, version increment, compensation remove, eligibility filtering, or Secretariat old-version check would leave the existing export-PDF assertions green → Verdict: the new immutable-document contract can regress silently, including duplicate versions, orphaned PDFs, and unauthorized final-document access. Add focused persistence/action tests for concurrent issuance, put/DB/cleanup failures, status eligibility, current-versus-history visibility, and download-ticket authorization/scope.
evidence: Premise: lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:16-43 implements write, version, and cleanup behavior → Path: a persistence failure or reissue occurs → Verdict: this new behavior needs direct failing-capable coverage.

Premise: app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:794-824 exports issued-document lookup, ticket, and history actions → Path: __tests__/admin-actions.test.ts imports actions at lines 64-81 → Verdict: none of those new actions are tested.

Premise: __tests__/admin-actions.test.ts:490-565 only asserts rendered PDF tokens and filename → Path: exportDecision succeeds with broken persistence → Verdict: artifact metadata and compensation regressions pass.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_03.md:95-118 requires versioning, compensation, authorization, current-document, and ticket coverage → Path: Task 03 is accepted → Verdict: the required tests are absent.

findings.title: Server accepts one uploaded file as every required document
findings.body: Premise: `uploadedPath` only tests the broad `pending/` prefix and absence of `..`, while every newly-required category is an independent array of that same schema. → Path: a direct `submitApplication` caller can upload one legitimate pending file (for example, a vacancy declaration) and repeat its path in `pai.documentos`, `mae.documentos`, `certidao_casamento`, address, income, bank, and both student arrays. `collectDocumentRows` then records that one file under each asserted category. → Verdict: direct Server Action submission bypasses the required distinct category contract, so an incomplete/fraudulent application is accepted despite the UI's separate fields.
findings.suggestion: Validate each submitted path against the expected pending category (and student index for student files), reject duplicate cross-category use, and retain that mapping when persisting document rows.
evidence: Premise: lib/validations/application-schema.ts:18-29 accepts only a broad pending path, not a field-specific category → Path: a direct submitApplication caller repeats one valid uploaded path in every required document array, which collectDocumentRows accepts at app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:252-290 → Verdict: the Server Action accepts an application without distinct required document categories.
lib/validations/application-schema.ts:18-29 → all required file arrays share a validator that does not inspect the category directory.
app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:252-290 → collectDocumentRows trusts the caller-selected payload field and assigns category metadata without checking the path's uploaded category.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_05.md requirements 5–8 and 15 → the Server Action must independently enforce each required category and only accept safe pending paths.

findings.title: Vincule os uploads ao tipo de documento exigido
findings.body: As duas listas distintas por aluno validam apenas que cada valor começa com `pending/`. Uma chamada direta pode usar o mesmo arquivo pendente em `documento_identidade` e `certidao_nascimento` (ou reutilizá-lo nos demais campos obrigatórios), de modo que o servidor aceita uma única evidência como ambos os documentos. Isso contorna justamente a separação obrigatória entre RG e certidão de nascimento.
evidence: Premise: lib/validations/application-schema.ts:19-24 accepts any non-traversal `pending/` string, and lines 36-37 apply that same schema independently to both student fields → Path: a direct `submitApplication` caller supplies the same existing pending path in both arrays → Verdict: one uploaded file passes both mandatory-document checks and is persisted as two categories.
app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:280-289 → collectDocumentRows trusts the already-validated arrays and labels their rows by field without verifying the ticket category or unique source path.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_05.md:requirements 5-8 → server validation must prevent direct calls from bypassing distinct, required document categories.

Premise: lib/validations/application-schema.ts:18-30 accepts any non-traversal pending path for every required array → Path: a direct caller can put one ticketed path into all required fields → Verdict: category-specific document requirements are bypassed.

Premise: app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:32-37 encodes a category into upload paths, including recibo_pagamento → Path: the generic schema predicate does not compare that encoded category with the receiving field → Verdict: a donor-receipt path can satisfy scholarship-document fields.

Premise: app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:277-291 relabels submitted paths as asserted document categories → Path: duplicated identical pending paths are moved after commit one row at a time → Verdict: the first move can leave later metadata rows referring to the old path.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_05.md:28-34 requires direct calls to enforce category-specific document requirements → Path: the new fields reuse the category-agnostic predicate → Verdict: the changed server contract does not meet its stated acceptance criterion.

advisories.title: Make upload-path fixtures match the production categories
advisories.body: The new fixture uses category segments that `createUploadUrl` never issues (`aluno_0_rg`, `aluno_0_certidao`), and the changed marriage path has the same problem (`certidao_casamento`). Keep schema fixtures representative of the transport contract so they can catch category-name drift between the form, ticket allowlist, and persisted document mapping.
evidence: Premise: __tests__/application-schema.test.ts:24,39-40 use `certidao_casamento`, `aluno_0_rg`, and `aluno_0_certidao` path segments → Improvement: the schema fixture will exercise the same category convention as real uploads → Fix: use `certidao`, `rg_aluno_0`, and `certidao_nascimento_0` in the corresponding fixture paths.
app/form/_components/step-2-students.tsx:186-205 → the form requests `rg_aluno_${i}` and `certidao_nascimento_${i}`.
app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:32-37 → the upload allowlist accepts `certidao` and only the `rg_aluno_<index>` / `certidao_nascimento_<index>` student patterns.

advisories.title: Make the administrator-capability test match its claim
advisories.body: The test says it grants every declared capability but exercises only `staff:manage`. Rename it to the capability it covers, or iterate the declared capability list, so a future capability cannot be mistakenly assumed covered.
evidence: Premise: __tests__/authorization.test.ts:84 names every declared capability, while line 92 invokes requireCapability only for staff:manage → Improvement: keeps the test name and its actual contract aligned → Fix: either rename the case or assert each Capability value.
lib/auth/authorization.ts:8-20 → Capability is a finite explicit union, so an exhaustive table-driven test is bounded.

advisories.title: Do not label the absent-user case as an Administrator guard
advisories.body: This setup makes `findFirst` return undefined, so both actions exit through their missing-user branch. The test name claims it protects an Administrator, which can mislead a future maintainer about what regression it catches. Rename the case to the missing/non-secretariat target behavior, or add a fake-DB predicate assertion that proves the secretaria role filter.
evidence: Premise: __tests__/staff-and-observations.test.ts:27 calls the scenario an Administrator case, but line 28 configures findFirst to return undefined → Improvement: makes the regression suite's stated protection truthful → Fix: rename it or assert the role-constrained lookup.
app/admin/_actions/staff-actions.ts:44-51 and 61-68 → production protection is the secretaria-constrained query, not an Administrator object returned by this test double.

advisories.title: Represent secretariat loading results with exported types instead of casts
advisories.body: The card casts both server-action results to local state types. Those casts conceal any contract drift in the operational projection, including relation nullability or a future document-field change. Export the small view-model types from the action/module (or derive state from Awaited<ReturnType<...>>) and type state to them so TypeScript checks the boundary.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:103-109 declares local anonymous state shapes and force-casts both Promise results → Improvement: type-checks the server-to-client operational projection rather than trusting it → Fix: export/reuse concrete observation and issued-document view-model types.
app/admin/_actions/observation-actions.ts:8-15 and app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:794-808 → both action return shapes are available at the boundary and can be named once.

Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:107-110 attaches only a then handler, while lines 112-123 ignore unsuccessful action results → Improvement: makes operational failures visible and retryable instead of silent → Fix: catch request failures and store/render an error state for loading, saving, and downloading.
app/admin/_actions/observation-actions.ts:22-36 and app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:810-821 → these actions deliberately return error variants that the component currently does not surface.

Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:100-136 contains the card's state, effects, handlers, and nested controls in a compact block unlike the established multiline component style below line 141 → Improvement: lowers review and modification cost for role-specific UI → Fix: expand the component and extract its repeated view fragments into readable JSX.
app/admin/benfeitores/client.tsx:93-101 and app/admin/_components/issued-documents.tsx:8-13 → the same compact style was introduced in the other new role/document views.

advisories.title: Expand the administration client into readable units
advisories.body: The three async mutations and the whole rendered interface are compressed into four very long lines. Splitting the handlers and JSX into normal blocks makes authorization/error-state changes reviewable and keeps later additions (pending state, confirmation, or field validation) local rather than editing a single dense expression.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/usuarios/client.tsx:13-16 places each mutation and most of the complete React tree on one line → Improvement: preserve meaningful handler and component boundaries for review and future edits → Fix: format the handlers and JSX into conventional multiline blocks without changing behavior.
app/admin/usuarios/client.tsx:8-17 → the full create, toggle, reset, and render flow is newly introduced in 10 physical lines.

advisories.title: Use the typed transaction query API instead of casting it to the root database
advisories.body: The double cast makes the relation query appear to be the root `db` inside a transaction, so future changes to the transaction or query shape can silently escape TypeScript's checking. Read the latest version with `tx.select(...).from(...).where(...).orderBy(...).limit(1)` and insert with `tx.insert(...)`; this keeps both operations visibly bound to the same typed transaction.
evidence: Premise: lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:20 casts `tx` through `unknown` to `typeof db` before querying → Improvement: retain compile-time transaction-bound query types → Fix: replace the relation query and cast with a direct `tx.select` query for the latest version.
lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:19-38 → the advisory lock, latest-version read, and insert are intended to run in the same transaction.

suppressions.candidate: Version allocation might race because it reads the previous version before inserting.
suppressions.note: The transaction takes a PostgreSQL advisory transaction lock keyed by application and kind before the latest-version read, so concurrent issuances of the same sequence serialize.

suppressions.candidate: Secretariat could fetch an old or ineligible issued document by ID.
suppressions.note: For Secretaria, getIssuedDocumentUrl recomputes current eligible documents and rejects IDs absent from that set; only Administrators may access history.

suppressions.candidate: The role-specific client branch is only a client-side authorization boundary.
suppressions.note: The page obtains a database-refreshed staff role and getApplications applies a server-side role projection; sensitive detail and export actions independently require Administrator.

suppressions.candidate: Documentation-only Go capability struct introduces an unrelated language example
suppressions.note: The immediately preceding text explicitly states that the Go struct exists solely for workflow-template compliance and does not introduce a runtime component; no local documentation change is warranted.

suppressions.candidate: Tasks 02 through 05 remain marked pending while implementation files are present
suppressions.note: The task records include incomplete acceptance checklists and the release is still undergoing verification, so their pending state is not stale tracking evidence.

suppressions.candidate: Task status remains pending while some implementation files exist
suppressions.note: These task files are planning and tracking artifacts; this lane cannot infer their intended completion state from the owned documentation hunks alone.

suppressions.candidate: Authorization mocks do not assert individual capability arguments
suppressions.note: The setup change is necessary to isolate actions after central authorization extraction, but proving an actionable missing assertion requires reviewing the action-specific tests outside this lane's owned hunks.

suppressions.candidate: Rename the local Document type because it shadows the DOM global
suppressions.note: The component does not use the DOM Document global, so the shadowing has no concrete local cost beyond preference.

suppressions.candidate: The upload-category allowlist could use an enum rather than strings.
suppressions.note: The categories form a small local server-side boundary and no observed caller ambiguity requires a broader type abstraction.

suppressions.candidate: Replace the native image element with next/image.
suppressions.note: The checked-in asset is a local SVG with explicit dimensions; no configured repository rule or observed benefit establishes that Next image optimization is required.

suppressions.candidate: Keep the removed disabled-upload API for possible reuse.
suppressions.note: The change intent explicitly re-enables mandatory uploads, so retaining a test-phase API would add dead surface rather than improve maintainability.

suppressions.candidate: Reformat Drizzle statement-breakpoint SQL into multiline statements.
suppressions.note: The migration uses the generator's conventional statement-breakpoint form; changing formatting alone has no bounded maintenance benefit.

suppressions.candidate: Drizzle snapshot contains verbose generated index and schema metadata
suppressions.note: The assigned file is Drizzle Kit's generated schema snapshot. Its repetitive representation is generator-owned; `npx drizzle-kit check --config=drizzle.config.ts` accepts the migration history, so there is no bounded hand-maintained polish change to make here.

suppressions.candidate: Reformat or hand-simplify generated Drizzle snapshot metadata
suppressions.note: The snapshot is Drizzle-generated migration metadata; schema and SQL are the maintainable sources reviewed elsewhere.

suppressions.candidate: Change generated journal entry layout or timestamp
suppressions.note: The journal entry is generated migration bookkeeping and matches migration index 0006.

suppressions.candidate: Enforce append-only observations with database-level mutation prevention
suppressions.note: No application caller in the inspected checkout updates or deletes observations; a database trigger would be a separate policy design rather than a bounded local polish change.

suppressions.candidate: Retain the temporary scholarship upload feature flag
suppressions.note: The implementation contract explicitly makes the enabled upload path the only supported behavior and removes the temporary gate.

suppressions.candidate: Replace the embedded image payload with an independently optimized asset
suppressions.note: The executable asset is an exact copy of the approved Open Design master, as required by the technical specification; altering it would require a separate approval of the brand asset.

suppressions.candidate: Session role or active status could be trusted after login
suppressions.note: requireStaff reads the session only for identity and reloads id, email, role and ativo from admin_users on every protected operation; inactive or missing rows are rejected before capability checks.

suppressions.candidate: Secretaria could receive full application or donor records through a direct Server Action call
suppressions.note: The operational actions independently require the capability and select explicit secretary-safe column projections; detailed applications, source documents, decisions, exports and donor management remain behind requireAdmin.

suppressions.candidate: Public upload URL creation could sign an arbitrary storage destination
suppressions.note: The category allowlist and generated UUID constrain every ticket to pending/{uuid}/{approved category}/{sanitized filename}; the upload route verifies the scope-specific HMAC and never accepts a destination from the request body.

suppressions.candidate: Secretaria could download arbitrary historical or ineligible issued documents by id
suppressions.note: The action reloads the issued-document row, re-evaluates the application status and current version set for Secretaria, and only then emits a short-lived download ticket; history remains requireAdmin.

suppressions.candidate: Download endpoint lacks a session check
suppressions.note: The endpoint is deliberately bearer-ticket based. It accepts only an unexpired HMAC ticket with the download scope; tickets are minted by protected actions and responses are private/no-store.

suppressions.candidate: NOT NULL role constraint could reject pre-existing admin accounts
suppressions.note: The migration first adds role as nullable, backfills every null role to admin at line 27, and only then adds the role check and NOT NULL constraint at lines 28-29. This is the ordered compatibility window required by task_01.md:24-26 and :51.

suppressions.candidate: Existing users could be deactivated during the additive account migration
suppressions.note: Adding ativo with DEFAULT true NOT NULL makes the existing row state and the new-record default agree with task_01.md:25-26. The migration changes neither IDs, emails, password hashes, nor applications.decided_by references.

suppressions.candidate: A failed multi-statement migration could leave a partial schema
suppressions.note: The configured postgres-js Drizzle migrator executes each pending migration inside one transaction before recording it in drizzle.__drizzle_migrations (node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:56-71), so any failing statement rolls back the migration rather than publishing a partial 0006 state.

suppressions.candidate: New foreign keys and indexes could remove or invalidate existing application data
suppressions.note: application_observations and issued_documents are newly created empty tables before their foreign keys and indexes are added. The migration does not recreate, delete from, or alter applications or existing application references; the only altered existing table is admin_users, handled by the preceding ordered backfill.

suppressions.candidate: Generated snapshot might not represent the SQL migration
suppressions.note: The generated snapshot records the same role check, new tables, foreign keys, uniqueness constraint, and indexes named by 0006 and lib/db/schema.ts. It is migration metadata rather than an independently owned executable implementation.

suppressions.candidate: Tests do not assert read ordering for application observations.
suppressions.note: This is part of the broader missing role/action matrix and immutable-document test coverage already reported; a separate finding would not identify a distinct root regression class.

suppressions.candidate: FSSPX footer text might clip at an unrendered breakpoint
suppressions.note: The full affiliation text exists and the inspected CSS supplies responsive one-column layout; without rendered viewport evidence this sweep cannot certify a concrete clipping failure.

suppressions.candidate: Concurrent issued-document versions could collide
suppressions.note: The transaction acquires a PostgreSQL advisory transaction lock keyed by application and kind before reading the latest version, which addresses the cross-request version race.

suppressions.candidate: Upload category allowlist permits traversal or unknown categories
suppressions.note: The fixed set plus anchored indexed-student regex at lines 32-37 reject separators, traversal text, and non-numeric indexes before ticket creation.

suppressions.candidate: Legacy scholarship route loses canonical routing behavior
suppressions.note: The legacy route contains only permanentRedirect to `/solicitar-bolsa`, while the canonical page declares `force-dynamic`.

suppressions.candidate: Concurrent issued-document versions can duplicate
suppressions.note: Issuance executes a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock on application and kind before reading the latest version, and the migration has the corresponding uniqueness constraint.
